variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Objective-C++ allows seamless mixing of C++ stack/heap objects and Objective-C heap objects in the same file (.mm extension).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: All C++ and Objective-C data types coexist. You can store pointers to Obj-C objects in C++ containers and vice versa.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: C++ features like operator overloading work normally on C++ objects, while Objective-C messaging continues to handle Obj-C objects.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are inherited from C and can freely mix standard library C++ operations with Foundation logging.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: You can use C++11 range-based loops for STL containers and Obj-C fast enumeration (for-in) for Foundation collections.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: While loops operate exactly as they do in C/C++.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions and methods can freely accept and return both C++ references/values and Objective-C object pointers.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: No direct bridging exists between STL vectors and NSArrays; manual iteration is required to convert between them.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: You can use std::map or std::unordered_map alongside NSDictionary. Mixing them requires manual data conversion.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: C++ uses try-catch exceptions, while Objective-C uses NSError pointers. They do not cross boundaries cleanly; catch C++ exceptions before letting them leak into Objective-C call stacks.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Objective-C++ provides comments to document code behavior.

numbers.title: Numbers & Constants
numbers.notes: Objective-C++ supports numeric literals for computation and indexing.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Objective-C++ provides boolean conditions for program control flow.

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Objective-C++ converts data between native format representations.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Objective-C++ represents textual data through string literals and character arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Objective-C++ formats and joins textual values for display and output.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Branching
pattern_matching.code:
case value of
    1: execute_one()
    default: execute_default()
pattern_matching.notes: Objective-C++ branches execution based on value comparison and conditional expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Intervals
range.notes: Objective-C++ defines intervals and index sequences for bounded processing.

iterators.title: Iteration & Loops
iterators.notes: Objective-C++ iterates across collections and sequence elements.

oop_classes.title: Structures & Modules
oop_classes.notes: Objective-C++ organizes data and behavior through structures or modular components.

lists.title: Collections & Arrays
lists.notes: Objective-C++ stores sequence data in indexed lists or arrays.

tuples.title: Records & Pairs
tuples.notes: Objective-C++ groups related fields into lightweight composite pairs or records.

sets.title: Sets & Uniqueness
sets.notes: Objective-C++ tracks unique values without duplicate entries.

modules_import.title: Libraries & Modules
modules_import.notes: Objective-C++ organizes external libraries and code units into modular namespaces.
